definition_en: attractive in a pretty or endearing way
core_image: 一只圆眼的小狗坐在篮子边，歪着头看人
scene: 一只圆眼的小狗坐在篮子边，歪着头看人。The puppy looks very cute.
sceneCN: 这里 cute 是「可爱的」（第 01 个义项）；句意是这只小狗看起来可爱极了。

senses.title: Pretty and endearing
senses.definition: attractive in a pretty or endearing way, especially a small animal or child
senses.definitionCN: 小巧、好看又让人心生喜爱的样子，多形容小动物或孩子
senses.example: The puppy looks very cute.
senses.exampleCN: 这只小狗看起来可爱极了。
senses.why: Cute is a shortened form of acute, which meant sharp; from "sharp-looking" it slid into "small and pleasing to look at".
senses.whyCN: cute 是 acute（尖锐的）的缩略形式，从「看起来机灵」滑向「小巧好看、讨人喜欢」。

senses.title: Clever in an annoying way
senses.definition: trying to be clever or tricky, in a way that annoys people
senses.definitionCN: 故意卖弄机灵、耍花招，让人不快
senses.example: Don't get cute with the teacher.
senses.exampleCN: 别跟老师耍小聪明。
senses.why: The "sharp" meaning inside cute survived: a person being cute is being too sharp, trying to outwit others instead of behaving plainly.
senses.whyCN: cute 里「尖锐」那层意思还在：说一个人 cute，就是说他太精，想靠小聪明压过别人。

definition_en: a bicycle, or a series of events that repeat
core_image: 一辆自行车靠在树旁，车轮的影子在地上画出一个圆
scene: 一辆自行车靠在树旁，车轮的影子在地上画出一个圆。He cycles to school every morning.
sceneCN: 这里 cycle 是「骑自行车」（第 03 个义项）；句意是他每天早上骑车上学。

senses.title: A bicycle
senses.definition: a bicycle, used especially in written or formal British English
senses.definitionCN: 自行车，多见于英国书面或正式说法
senses.example: He cycles to school every morning.
senses.exampleCN: 他每天早上骑车上学。
senses.why: Greek kyklos, a circle, gave English cycle; the two-wheeled machine was named for its wheels going round, and the short noun kept that name.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 kyklos「圆」演变出 cycle；两个轮子转圈的车因此得名，名词形式保留了这个称呼。

senses.title: A series of events that repeats
senses.definition: a set of events that happen again and again in the same order
senses.definitionCN: 按同样顺序反复出现的一串事情
senses.example: The seasons follow a yearly cycle.
senses.exampleCN: 四季按一年的周期循环。
senses.why: The original sense of kyklos was a circle, and a circle returns to where it started, so any repeating round of events is a cycle.
senses.whyCN: kyklos 本义是圆圈，圆圈走一圈又回到起点，所以任何反复一轮的事情都叫 cycle。

senses.title: To ride a bicycle
senses.definition: to travel by bicycle
senses.definitionCN: 骑自行车出行
senses.example: She cycles to the park on Sundays.
senses.exampleCN: 她星期天骑车去公园。
senses.why: The verb simply turns the bicycle noun into the action of using it, the way many vehicle names become verbs.
senses.whyCN: 动词只是把「自行车」这个名词变成使用它的动作，很多交通工具名称都这样转化为动词。

definition_en: a period of twenty-four hours, or the time when it is light
core_image: 窗帘拉开，阳光照进房间，窗外的街道开始有人走动
scene: 窗帘拉开，阳光照进房间，窗外的街道开始有人走动。The day begins with a bright sunrise.
sceneCN: 这里 day 是「白天」（第 02 个义项）；句意是白天从明亮的日出开始。

senses.title: A period of twenty-four hours
senses.definition: a period of twenty-four hours, measured from midnight to midnight
senses.definitionCN: 从午夜到午夜的一段时间
senses.example: She spent three days on the project.
senses.exampleCN: 她在这个项目上花了三天。
senses.why: Old English dæg named the whole span of a day, and that counting sense survives in phrases like three days and every day.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 dæg 指完整的一天，这个用来计数的意思保留在 three days、every day 这类说法里。

senses.title: The time when it is light
senses.definition: the hours between sunrise and sunset, when there is daylight
senses.definitionCN: 日出到日落之间、天亮的那些小时
senses.example: The day begins with a bright sunrise.
senses.exampleCN: 白天从明亮的日出开始。
senses.why: The same word split the twenty-four hours into light and dark, and day took the light half while night took the rest.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词把二十四小时分成明暗两半，day 拿到天亮的那一半，其余归 night。

senses.title: A particular date or occasion
senses.definition: a particular date, often one marked by an event or celebration
senses.definitionCN: 某个特定日期，常带活动或庆祝
senses.example: Sports day is next Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 运动会在下周五。
senses.why: Because a day is a marked unit on the calendar, it also names the date set aside for something, as in sports day or National Day.
senses.whyCN: 一天是日历上一个标好的单位，于是也用来指名目专门定下的那个日子，如 sports day、National Day。

definition_en: a unit of measurement, an amount, or an academic rank
core_image: 墙上的温度计指针停在三十度，窗外是烈日
scene: 墙上的温度计指针停在三十度，窗外是烈日。The thermometer shows thirty degrees.
sceneCN: 这里 degree 是「度」（第 01 个义项）；句意是温度计显示三十度。

senses.title: A unit for measuring temperature or angles
senses.definition: a unit marked on a scale for measuring temperature or angles
senses.definitionCN: 温度计或角度刻度上的计量单位
senses.example: The thermometer shows thirty degrees.
senses.exampleCN: 温度计显示三十度。
senses.why: Latin de- plus gradus, a step, gave degree, one step on a scale; a thermometer is such a scale, so each mark is a degree.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 de- 加 gradus「台阶」构成 degree，即刻度上的一格；温度计正是这样一把刻度尺，每一格就是一度。

senses.title: The amount or level of something
senses.definition: the amount, level or extent to which something is true
senses.definitionCN: 某事成立的程度或深浅
senses.example: The two stories differ in degree, not in kind.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个说法差别在程度上，不在性质上。
senses.why: A step on a scale also measures how far something has gone, so degree came to mean the extent of a quality rather than a fixed unit.
senses.whyCN: 刻度上的一格也量出某事物走到了多远，于是 degree 从固定单位引申为某种性质的程度。

senses.title: An academic rank from a university
senses.definition: a rank given by a university to someone who has completed a course of study
senses.definitionCN: 大学授予完成学业者的学术等级
senses.example: She has a degree in history.
senses.exampleCN: 她有一个历史学学位。
senses.why: University study was once organised as a series of graded steps, and the rank reached at the end kept the name degree.
senses.whyCN: 大学学业曾按一级一级的台阶组织，走到终点所获的等级就沿用了 degree 这个名字。

core_image: 一盘刚出炉的蛋糕放在桌上，热气带着甜香飘起来
scene: 一盘刚出炉的蛋糕放在桌上，热气带着甜香飘起来。The cake smells delicious.
sceneCN: 这里 delicious 是「美味的」（第 01 个义项）；句意是这蛋糕闻起来真香。

senses.title: Tasting or smelling very good
senses.definition: having a very pleasant taste or smell
senses.definitionCN: 吃起来或闻起来非常可口
senses.example: The cake smells delicious.
senses.exampleCN: 这蛋糕闻起来真香。
senses.why: Latin deliciae meant delight, and delicious kept the idea of pleasure taken in through the senses of taste and smell.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 deliciae 意为愉悦，delicious 保留了通过味觉和嗅觉获得快乐这层意思。

senses.title: Very pleasant in a non-food way
senses.titleCN: 令人愉快的；妙不可言的
senses.definition: extremely pleasant or enjoyable, used figuratively about things that are not food
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法，形容食物之外的事物非常有意思
senses.example: The story has a delicious twist.
senses.exampleCN: 这个故事有一个妙不可言的转折。
senses.why: The pleasure of a good meal was borrowed for other delights, so a delicious twist gives the mind the same kind of enjoyment.
senses.whyCN: 一顿美餐带来的快乐被借去形容别的愉快，于是 a delicious twist 给脑子同样的享受。

definition_en: a book in which you write about your days
core_image: 床头柜上放着一个带锁的小本子，封面夹着一支笔
scene: 床头柜上放着一个带锁的小本子，封面夹着一支笔。She writes in her diary before bed.
sceneCN: 这里 diary 是「日记本」（第 01 个义项）；句意是她睡前在日记本上写几行。

senses.title: A book with a page for each day
senses.definition: a book with a space or page for each day of the year
senses.definitionCN: 按日期一页一天的本子
senses.example: She writes in her diary before bed.
senses.exampleCN: 她睡前在日记本上写几行。
senses.why: Latin dies, day, gave diarium, a daily allowance or record, and English kept it for the book that holds one page per day.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 dies「日」构成 diarium，指按日分配的记录，英语用它指一天一页的本子。

senses.title: A daily record of your life
senses.definition: the daily record itself, written in such a book
senses.definitionCN: 写在这种本子里的逐日记录
senses.example: His diary tells what he did each day.
senses.exampleCN: 他的日记记下他每天做了什么。
senses.why: The container and the contents share one name: the same word that names the book also names what is written inside it.
senses.whyCN: 本子和内容共用同一个名字：指本子的词，也指写在里面的记录。

senses.title: A book for planning appointments
senses.definition: a book in which you write appointments and things to do
senses.definitionCN: 用来记约会和待办事项的本子
senses.example: She checked her diary for the meeting time.
senses.exampleCN: 她翻了翻日程本，看会议时间。
senses.why: In British use the dated book was turned to planning ahead, so diary also names the book that holds future appointments.

senses.title: The main meal of the day

core_image: 博物馆里一具高大的恐龙骨架，孩子在它脚下仰头看

senses.title: A large extinct animal of the distant past
senses.definition: a large animal with four legs and a long tail that lived millions of years ago and is now extinct
senses.definitionCN: 数百万年前生活、如今已灭绝的大型四足长尾动物
senses.example: A dinosaur skeleton stands in the museum hall.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆大厅里立着一具恐龙骨架。
senses.why: Greek deinos, terrible, plus sauros, lizard, gave dinosaur, the "terrible lizard" named by a Victorian scientist for the giant fossil bones.

senses.title: Someone or something hopelessly out of date

senses.example: The old typewriter is a dinosaur in a modern office.
senses.exampleCN: 在现代办公室里，那台旧打字机是个老古董。
senses.why: Dinosaurs died out while the world changed, so the name became a metaphor for anything that cannot keep up and disappears.
senses.whyCN: 恐龙在世界改变时灭绝了，这个名字就被用来比喻跟不上变化、终将消失的事物。

definition_en: covered with dirt, or to make something dirty
core_image: 一双沾满泥的球鞋放在门口，旁边是干净的地板
scene: 一双沾满泥的球鞋放在门口，旁边是干净的地板。His shoes are dirty after the rain.
sceneCN: 这里 dirty 是「脏的」（第 01 个义项）；句意是雨后他的鞋很脏。

senses.title: Covered with dirt
senses.definition: covered or marked with dirt, dust or stains
senses.definitionCN: 沾上泥土、灰尘或污渍
senses.example: His shoes are dirty after the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 雨后他的鞋很脏。
senses.why: Dirt came from Old Norse drit, filth, and the adjective simply says that something is covered with it.
senses.whyCN: dirt 来自古北欧语 drit「污物」，形容词直接表示某物沾满了这种东西。

senses.title: To make something dirty
senses.definition: to get dirt or stains onto something
senses.definitionCN: 把泥土或污渍弄到某物上
senses.example: The mud dirtied her white dress.
senses.exampleCN: 泥巴弄脏了她的白裙子。
senses.why: The adjective turned into a verb: making something dirty is putting dirt where it was clean.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转成动词：让东西变脏，就是把污物带到原本干净的地方。

senses.title: Unfair or dishonest
senses.definition: unfair, dishonest or cruel, used about actions and tricks
senses.definitionCN: 形容手段不公平、不诚实或阴损
senses.example: It was a dirty trick to hide her shoes.
senses.exampleCN: 把她的鞋藏起来是个卑劣的把戏。
senses.why: Filth was long used as an image for moral foulness, so a dirty trick is a trick that leaves the same stain on the people who play it.
senses.whyCN: 污秽历来被用来比喻道德上的败坏，所以 dirty trick 就是会让使坏者自己也沾上污点的把戏。

definition_en: to perform an action or task
core_image: 书桌上摊着作业本和铅笔，孩子正一行行写字
scene: 书桌上摊着作业本和铅笔，孩子正一行行写字。They do their homework together.
sceneCN: 这里 do 是「做」（第 01 个义项）；句意是他们一起做作业。

pos.zh: 助动词：用于疑问与否定

senses.title: To perform an action or task
senses.definition: to carry out an action, job or piece of work
senses.definitionCN: 执行某个动作、活儿或任务
senses.example: They do their homework together.
senses.exampleCN: 他们一起做作业。
senses.why: Old English dōn was the general verb for carrying out anything, and it still fills that role when no more specific verb is needed.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 dōn 是表示「执行」的万能动词，在找不到更具体的动词时，它仍旧顶上这个位置。

senses.title: Used to form questions and negatives
senses.definition: used with another verb to form questions, negatives and emphasis
senses.definitionCN: 与实义动词连用，构成疑问、否定或强调
senses.example: Do you like this song?
senses.exampleCN: 你喜欢这首歌吗？
senses.why: English needed a helper to build questions, and the general verb do was chosen; in this role it carries no meaning of its own.
senses.whyCN: 英语需要一个帮手来构造疑问句，于是选中了万能动词 do；在这个位置上它本身不携带词义。

senses.title: To be enough or acceptable
senses.definition: to be enough for a purpose, or to be acceptable
senses.definitionCN: 足够应付某个用途，或可以接受
senses.example: That will do for now.
senses.exampleCN: 目前这样就行了。
senses.why: If a thing "does", it has performed what was asked of it, so do came to mean that something meets the need and no more is required.
senses.whyCN: 一样东西「do」，就是它把要求的事做到了，于是 do 引申为「够用、可以了」，不必再多。
